perspective:
Ethan Mohamud’s available information:

- Ethan is a plumber. Gary Guo is his long-time friend, a doctor, whom he has known since middle school.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. This concerned him.
- Ethan invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation. Gary initially declined, saying he appreciated the concern but had too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than professional obligations.
- Ethan told Gary they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary replied that it was complicated and he did not want to burden Ethan.
- Gary opened up to Ethan about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating some responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and remaining challenges. Ethan saw Gary making efforts to change.
- Gary told Ethan things were better, thanked him for his help, said he was less overwhelmed, and mentioned he had had time for a movie the previous weekend.
- Ethan told Gary he was proud of his progress and reminded him he was available whenever Gary needed to talk.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing on his own. Ethan told Gary he was always just a call away and that he knew Gary had this. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and said he felt more in control.
